contributions: An affordable, open-source alternative to expensive traditional discrete mathematics textbooks
Updates the 2nd edition (1989) of Applied Discrete Structures for Computer Science for 21st-century computing by replacing Pascal with SageMath

Provides a comprehensive two-semester course text covering set theory, combinatorics, logic, matrices, relations, functions, recursion, graph theory, trees, algebraic structures, Boolean algebra, automata, group theory, and ring theory
limitations: The text acknowledges that Pascal, while not 'totally dead,' is far from mainstream in 21st-century computing, requiring a shift to SageMath
The empty set's status as a proper subset is noted as a point of disagreement in the mathematical community, with earlier editions taking a different position
The definition of 'finite' is left undefined, and a proper definition of real numbers is stated to be beyond the scope of the text
Cardinality is restricted to finite sets until Chapter 7, deferring discussion of different infinite cardinalities
methods: The authors redeveloped an earlier textbook (originally published with Science Research Associates in 1988, later rights held by Pearson) as an open-source project starting in 2010. The text was developed using PreTeXt, a lightweight XML application for scientific authors. The 1980s-era Pascal programming examples were replaced with SageMath, an open-source computer algebra system released in 2005. Financial assistance was provided by the Pedagogy Subcommittee of the UMass Lowell Transformational Education Committee.
results: The book covers 16 chapters spanning set theory, combinatorics, logic, matrix algebra, relations, functions and probability, recursion, graph theory, trees, algebraic structures, Boolean algebra, monoids and automata, group theory, and rings/fields, with appendices on algorithms, Python and SageMath, determinants, notation, and a glossary. It includes hints and solutions to selected exercises. The original text was peer-reviewed and adopted at several universities. Many students provided feedback and identified typos across editions.
tldr: Applied Discrete Structures is an open-source textbook for university-level discrete mathematics, originally designed for computer science and math majors, updated from a 1989/2008 text and developed using PreTeXt with SageMath replacing Pascal.
